# minuta

> Divide time into pieces: pure functions over plain, deeply readonly `Period` data (`{ start, end, unit }`, `end` inclusive), with the date engine plugged in as data ("units").

## Rules

- Every unit-aware function exists twice: `xWith(units, …)` in `minuta/core` takes the units first; `x(…)` in `minuta` is the same function bound to the native `Date` units with weeks starting on Monday. Unit-free functions have one form and take no units.
- `withUnits(units, { plugins })` (from `minuta/core`) binds every operation, and the functions of plugins such as `calendar` from `minuta/calendar`, to your units, e.g. `withUnits(nativeUnits({ weekStartsOn: "sunday" }), { plugins: [calendar] })`; the result's `units` are the units passed in. `bind(units, plugin)` binds a plugin on its own.
- `Units` is a partial map of unit specs; pass only the units you use (`{ day, month }`) to keep the bundle small.
- No result is `undefined`, never `null` (`clamp` without overlap, `merge([])`, …).
- Invalid input throws `RangeError`; the message starts with one of the error codes below and says how to fix it.
- Nothing is mutated: every function returns new data.

## Error codes

- `INVALID_DATE`: A Date argument is invalid (`new Date("nope")`).
- `INVALID_OPTION`: An option such as `step` or `maxPeriods` is not a positive whole number.
- `TOO_MANY_PERIODS`: `divideWith` would create more chunks than `maxPeriods` allows.
- `UNIT_NOT_SUPPORTED`: The `units` passed to a function have no spec for the requested unit.

## `minuta`

### `divide`

```ts
divide(period: Period, unit: Unit, options: DivideOptions = {}): Period[]
```

Split a period into chunks of `unit`, clipped to the period. Native units,
weeks start on Monday; `divideWith` in `minuta/core` takes your own units.

```ts
divide(period(new Date(2026, 2, 1), "month"), "day"); // 31 day periods
divide(period(new Date(2026, 2, 1, 9), "hour"), "minute", { step: 15 }); // 4 periods
```

### `duration`

```ts
duration(period: Period, unit: Unit): number
```

How many complete `unit`s fit into a period. Native units, calendar- and
DST-aware; `durationWith` in `minuta/core` takes your own units.

```ts
duration(period(new Date(2026, 9, 8), "day"), "hour"); // 24
duration(period(new Date(2026, 1, 1), "month"), "day"); // 28
```

### `isToday`

```ts
isToday(now: Readonly<Date>, period: Period): boolean
```

Whether `period` is the day containing `now`. Native units.

```ts
isToday(new Date(), period(new Date(), "day")); // true
```

### `isWeekday`

```ts
isWeekday(period: Period): boolean
```

Whether every day the period touches is a working day (Monday to Friday).
Native units; for another weekend use `withUnits(nativeUnits({ weekend }))`.

```ts
isWeekday(period(new Date(2026, 2, 18), "day")); // true (a Wednesday)
```

### `isWeekend`

```ts
isWeekend(period: Period): boolean
```

Whether every day the period touches is Saturday or Sunday. Native units;
for another weekend use `withUnits(nativeUnits({ weekend }))`.

```ts
isWeekend(period(new Date(2026, 2, 21), "day")); // true (a Saturday)
```

### `merge`

```ts
merge(periods: readonly Period[], unit?: Unit): Period | undefined
```

Merge periods into one; keeps `unit` only when the result is exactly one
period of it, otherwise `"custom"`. Native units.

```ts
merge([period(new Date(2026, 0, 5), "day"), period(new Date(2026, 0, 9), "day")]); // Jan 5–9, "custom"
merge(divide(period(new Date(2026, 0, 1), "month"), "day"), "month"); // January, "month"
```

### `next`

```ts
next(period: Period): Period
```

The next period of the same unit. Native units, weeks start on Monday.

```ts
next(period(new Date(2026, 2, 15), "month")); // April 2026
```

### `period`

```ts
period(date: Readonly<Date>, unit: Unit): Period
```

The period of `unit` that contains `date`. Native units, weeks start on
Monday; `periodWith` in `minuta/core` takes your own units.

```ts
period(new Date(2026, 2, 15), "month"); // { start: Mar 1, end: Mar 31 23:59:59.999, unit: "month" }
period(new Date(2026, 2, 18), "week"); // Monday Mar 16 to Sunday Mar 22
```

### `previous`

```ts
previous(period: Period): Period
```

The previous period of the same unit. Native units, weeks start on Monday.

```ts
previous(period(new Date(2026, 2, 15), "month")); // February 2026
```

### `same`

```ts
same(first: Period, second: Period, unit: Unit | "custom"): boolean
```

Whether two periods fall into the same `unit`. Native units.

```ts
same(period(new Date(2026, 2, 16), "day"), period(new Date(2026, 2, 20), "day"), "week"); // true
```

### `shift`

```ts
shift(period: Period, steps: number): Period
```

Move a period by `steps` of its own unit; negative moves back. Native units.

```ts
shift(period(new Date(2026, 2, 15), "month"), 3); // June 2026
```

### `snap`

```ts
snap(date: Readonly<Date>, unit: Unit, options: SnapOptions = {}): Date
```

Snap a date to a boundary of `step` units. Native units, weeks start on
Monday; `snapWith` in `minuta/core` takes your own units.

```ts
snap(new Date(2026, 2, 15, 10, 37), "minute", { step: 15 }); // 10:30
snap(new Date(2026, 2, 15, 10, 37), "hour", { mode: "ceil" }); // 11:00
```

### `clamp`

```ts
clamp(period: Period, bounds: Period): Period | undefined
```

Constrain a period to fit within bounds.

Returns undefined if the period is entirely outside bounds.

```ts
const selection = range(new Date(2026, 0, 5), new Date(2026, 0, 25))
const allowed = range(new Date(2026, 0, 10), new Date(2026, 0, 20))
clamp(selection, allowed)
// → { start: Jan 10, end: Jan 20, unit: "custom" }
```

### `contains`

```ts
contains(period: Period, target: Readonly<Date> | Period): boolean
```

Check if a period contains a date or another period.

```ts
contains(period(new Date(2026, 2, 1), "month"), new Date(2026, 2, 20)); // true
contains(period(new Date(2026, 2, 1), "month"), period(new Date(2026, 3, 1), "day")); // false
```

### `gap`

```ts
gap(from: TimePoint, to: TimePoint): Period | undefined
```

The time strictly between two dates or periods: from the millisecond after
the earlier one ends to the millisecond before the later one starts. A date
counts as its own millisecond. Order does not matter.

```ts
gap(period(new Date(2026, 2, 2), "day"), period(new Date(2026, 2, 5), "day"));
// { start: Mar 3, end: Mar 4 23:59:59.999, unit: "custom" }
gap(period(new Date(2026, 2, 2), "day"), period(new Date(2026, 2, 3), "day")); // undefined: they touch
```

### `length`

```ts
length(period: Period): number
```

The period's length in milliseconds, measured over the half-open range
`[start, end + 1 ms)`, so a whole day is exactly one day long.

```ts
length(period(new Date(2026, 9, 8), "day")); // 86400000, outside a DST change
```

### `move`

```ts
move(period: Period, targetDate: Readonly<Date>): Period
```

Relocate a period to a target date, preserving its duration.

```ts
const appointment = range(new Date(2026, 2, 29, 9, 0), new Date(2026, 2, 29, 10, 0))
const relocated = move(appointment, new Date(2026, 3, 2, 14, 0))
// → { start: Apr 2 14:00, end: Apr 2 15:00, unit: "custom" }
```

### `overlaps`

```ts
overlaps(first: Period, second: Period): boolean
```

Checks if two periods share any time.

```ts
overlaps(range(new Date(2026, 2, 1), new Date(2026, 2, 10)), range(new Date(2026, 2, 5), new Date(2026, 2, 20))); // true
```

### `range`

```ts
range(start: Readonly<Date>, end: Readonly<Date>): Period
```

A custom period from `start` to `end` (inclusive). Forgiving: dates given in
reverse order are swapped.

```ts
range(new Date(2026, 0, 1), new Date(2026, 2, 31))
// { start: Jan 1, end: Mar 31, unit: "custom" }
```

### `resize`

```ts
resize(period: Period, edge: "start" | "end", newDate: Readonly<Date>): Period | undefined
```

Move one edge of a period while keeping the other fixed.

Returns undefined if the new edge crosses the fixed edge.

```ts
const meeting = range(new Date(2026, 2, 29, 9, 0), new Date(2026, 2, 29, 10, 0))
resize(meeting, 'end', new Date(2026, 2, 29, 11, 30))
// → { start: 9:00, end: 11:30, unit: "custom" }
```

### `split`

```ts
split(period: Period, splitDate: Readonly<Date>): [Period, Period] | undefined
```

Split a period at a date inside it. Both parts are `"custom"` periods:
half a month is not a month.

```ts
const parts = split(period(new Date(2026, 2, 1), "month"), new Date(2026, 2, 15));
// [Mar 1 – Mar 14 23:59:59.999, Mar 15 – Mar 31 23:59:59.999]
split(period(new Date(2026, 2, 1), "month"), new Date(2027, 0, 1)); // undefined
```

### `MinutaError`

Codes at the start of the messages of errors minuta throws.

### `MinutaErrorCode`

```ts
type MinutaErrorCode = (typeof MinutaError)[keyof typeof MinutaError];
```

One of the {@link MinutaError} codes.

### `DivideOptions`

```ts
type DivideOptions = Readonly<{
  /** Maximum number of periods before throwing. Default: 100,000. */
  maxPeriods?: number | undefined;
  /** How many units each chunk spans. Default: 1. */
  step?: number | undefined;
}>;
```

Options for `divide` / `divideWith`.

### `SnapMode`

```ts
type SnapMode = "ceil" | "floor" | "nearest";
```

How `snap` / `snapWith` picks the boundary.

### `SnapOptions`

```ts
type SnapOptions = Readonly<{
  /** `"floor"`, `"ceil"` or `"nearest"` (ties round up). Default: `"nearest"`. */
  mode?: SnapMode | undefined;
  /** How many units lie between boundaries. Default: 1. */
  step?: number | undefined;
}>;
```

Options for `snap` / `snapWith`.

### `Minuta`

```ts
type Minuta = Readonly<{
  clamp: typeof clamp;
  contains: typeof contains;
  divide: Bound<typeof divideWith>;
  duration: Bound<typeof durationWith>;
  gap: typeof gap;
  isToday: Bound<typeof isTodayWith>;
  isWeekday: Bound<typeof isWeekdayWith>;
  isWeekend: Bound<typeof isWeekendWith>;
  length: typeof length;
  merge: Bound<typeof mergeWith>;
  move: typeof move;
  next: Bound<typeof nextWith>;
  overlaps: typeof overlaps;
  period: Bound<typeof periodWith>;
  previous: Bound<typeof previousWith>;
  range: typeof range;
  resize: typeof resize;
  same: Bound<typeof sameWith>;
  shift: Bound<typeof shiftWith>;
  snap: Bound<typeof snapWith>;
  split: typeof split;
  /** The units every member is bound to */
  units: Units;
}>;
```

All operations, bound to one set of units.

### `Period`

```ts
type Period = Readonly<{
  end: Readonly<Date>;
  start: Readonly<Date>;
  unit: Unit | "custom";
}>;
```

The primitive: every time range is a Period. Plain, deeply readonly data.

`periodWith(units, date, "month")` creates one aligned to a unit,
`range(start, end)` a custom one. `end` is inclusive (the last millisecond).

### `Series`

```ts
type Series = Readonly<{
  periods: readonly Period[];
}>;
```

A container of periods. Calendar grids extend it with metadata.

### `Unit`

```ts
type Unit = keyof UnitRegistry;
```

A unit name: `"year"`, `"quarter"`, `"month"`, `"week"`, `"day"`, `"hour"`,
`"minute"` or `"second"`, plus any unit added to `UnitRegistry`.

### `Units`

```ts
type Units = Readonly<Partial<Record<Unit, UnitSpec>>> & Settings;
```

The unit specs available to unit-aware functions. Partial, so a bundle can
carry only the units it uses; adapters such as `nativeUnits()` return all,
plus the `weekend`.

### `Weekday`

```ts
type Weekday =
  | "friday"
  | "monday"
  | "saturday"
  | "sunday"
  | "thursday"
  | "tuesday"
  | "wednesday";
```

A day of the week by name.

## `minuta/core`

### `clamp`

Same as `clamp` in `minuta`.

### `contains`

Same as `contains` in `minuta`.

### `divideWith`

```ts
divideWith(units: Units, period: Period, unit: Unit, options: DivideOptions = {}): Period[]
```

Divide a period into chunks of `unit`, clipped to the period.

```ts
divideWith(units, month, "day")                 // 28-31 day periods
divideWith(units, hour, "minute", { step: 15 }) // 4 fifteen-minute periods
```

### `durationWith`

```ts
durationWith(units: Units, period: Period, unit: Unit): number
```

How many complete `unit`s fit into a period, measured over the half-open
range `[start, end + 1 ms)` with the units' own calendar and DST rules.

```ts
durationWith(units, period(new Date(2026, 9, 8), "day"), "hour"); // 24
durationWith(units, period(new Date(2026, 1, 1), "month"), "day"); // 28
```

### `gap`

Same as `gap` in `minuta`.

### `isTodayWith`

```ts
isTodayWith(units: Units, now: Readonly<Date>, period: Period): boolean
```

Whether `period` is the day that contains `now`.

```ts
isTodayWith(nativeUnits(), new Date(), periodWith(nativeUnits(), new Date(), "day")); // true
```

### `isWeekdayWith`

```ts
isWeekdayWith(units: Units, period: Period): boolean
```

Whether every day the period touches is a working day: not in the units'
`weekend` (Saturday and Sunday unless set).

```ts
isWeekdayWith(nativeUnits(), period(new Date(2026, 2, 18), "day")); // true (a Wednesday)
isWeekdayWith(nativeUnits({ weekend: ["friday", "saturday"] }), period(new Date(2026, 2, 22), "day")); // true (a Sunday)
```

### `isWeekendWith`

```ts
isWeekendWith(units: Units, period: Period): boolean
```

Whether every day the period touches is a weekend day, as configured by
the units' `weekend` (Saturday and Sunday unless set).

```ts
isWeekendWith(nativeUnits(), period(new Date(2026, 2, 21), "day")); // true (a Saturday)
isWeekendWith(nativeUnits({ weekend: ["friday", "saturday"] }), period(new Date(2026, 2, 20), "day")); // true (a Friday)
```

### `length`

Same as `length` in `minuta`.

### `mergeWith`

```ts
mergeWith(units: Units, periods: readonly Period[], unit?: Unit): Period | undefined
```

Merge periods into one spanning the earliest start to the latest end. The
result keeps `unit` (by default the first period's unit) only when it is
exactly one period of that unit; otherwise its unit is `"custom"`.

```ts
mergeWith(units, [januaryFirstHalf, januarySecondHalf], "month"); // January, unit "month"
mergeWith(units, [january, march]); // Jan 1 – Mar 31, unit "custom"
mergeWith(units, []); // undefined
```

### `move`

Same as `move` in `minuta`.

### `nextWith`

```ts
nextWith(units: Units, period: Period): Period
```

The next period of the same unit.

```ts
nextWith(nativeUnits(), periodWith(nativeUnits(), new Date(2026, 2, 15), "month")); // April 2026
```

### `overlaps`

Same as `overlaps` in `minuta`.

### `periodWith`

```ts
periodWith(units: Units, date: Readonly<Date>, unit: Unit): Period
```

The period of `unit` that contains `date`.

```ts
periodWith(units, new Date(2026, 2, 15), "month")
// { start: Mar 1 00:00, end: Mar 31 23:59:59.999, unit: "month" }
```

### `previousWith`

```ts
previousWith(units: Units, period: Period): Period
```

The previous period of the same unit.

```ts
previousWith(nativeUnits(), periodWith(nativeUnits(), new Date(2026, 2, 15), "month")); // February 2026
```

### `range`

Same as `range` in `minuta`.

### `resize`

Same as `resize` in `minuta`.

### `sameWith`

```ts
sameWith(units: Units, first: Period, second: Period, unit: Unit | "custom"): boolean
```

Whether two periods fall into the same `unit` (compared by their starts).
With `"custom"`, both edges must be identical.

```ts
sameWith(units, mondayPeriod, fridayPeriod, "week") // true
```

### `shiftWith`

```ts
shiftWith(units: Units, period: Period, steps: number): Period
```

Move a period by `steps` of its own unit. A custom period moves by its own
length.

```ts
shiftWith(units, march, 2)  // May
shiftWith(units, march, -1) // February
```

### `snapWith`

```ts
snapWith(units: Units, date: Readonly<Date>, unit: Unit, options: SnapOptions = {}): Date
```

Snap a date to a boundary of `step` units: the unit's start, or every
`step`-th one counted from the start of the enclosing unit (minutes from
the hour, hours from the day, days from the month, months and quarters
from the year; weeks and years from 1970).

```ts
snapWith(units, new Date(2026, 2, 15, 10, 37), "minute", { step: 15 }); // 10:30
snapWith(units, new Date(2026, 2, 15, 10, 37), "day", { mode: "ceil" }); // Mar 16
snapWith(units, new Date(2026, 2, 18), "week", { mode: "floor" }); // the week's start
```

### `split`

Same as `split` in `minuta`.

### `bind`

```ts
bind(units: Units, plugin: Functions): BoundPlugin<Functions>
```

Bind every function of `plugin` to `units`.

```ts
import { calendar } from "minuta/calendar";
const grids = bind(nativeUnits({ weekStartsOn: "sunday" }), calendar);
grids.monthGrid(new Date());
```

### `MinutaError`

Same as `MinutaError` in `minuta`.

### `specFor`

```ts
specFor(units: Units, unit: Unit): UnitSpec
```

The spec for `unit`.

```ts
specFor(nativeUnits(), "week").startOf(new Date(2026, 2, 18)); // Monday Mar 16, 00:00
```

### `MinutaErrorCode`

Same as `MinutaErrorCode` in `minuta`.

### `withUnits`

```ts
withUnits(units: Units, options: WithUnitsOptions<Plugins> & NoClashes<Plugins> = {}): Minuta & BoundPlugins<Plugins>
```

Bind every operation, and the functions of any plugins, to `units`. Pass
only the units you need, or an adapter's full set.

```ts
import { calendar } from "minuta/calendar";
import { nativeUnits } from "minuta/native";
import { withUnits } from "minuta/core";

const time = withUnits(nativeUnits({ weekStartsOn: "sunday" }), { plugins: [calendar] });
time.next(time.period(new Date(), "week"));
time.monthGrid(new Date()); // from the plugin
time.units; // the units passed in
```

### `Bound`

```ts
type Bound<Fn> = Fn extends (units: Units, ...args: infer Args) => infer Result
  ? (...args: Args) => Result
  : never;
```

`Fn` without its leading `units` parameter.

### `BoundPlugin`

```ts
type BoundPlugin<Functions> = Readonly<{
  [Name in keyof Functions]: Bound<Functions[Name]>;
}>;
```

Every function of a plugin, bound to one set of units.

### `Plugin`

```ts
type Plugin = Readonly<Record<string, WithUnits>>;
```

An object of context-first functions, such as `calendar`.

### `WithUnits`

```ts
type WithUnits = (units: Units, ...args: readonly never[]) => unknown;
```

A context-first function: unit specs first, then its own arguments.

### `DivideOptions`

Same as `DivideOptions` in `minuta`.

### `SnapMode`

Same as `SnapMode` in `minuta`.

### `SnapOptions`

Same as `SnapOptions` in `minuta`.

### `Minuta`

Same as `Minuta` in `minuta`.

### `WithUnitsOptions`

```ts
type WithUnitsOptions<Plugins extends readonly Plugin[]> = Readonly<{
  /** Plugins whose functions join the result, bound to the same units */
  plugins?: Plugins | undefined;
}>;
```

Options of `withUnits`.

### `WeekOptions`

```ts
type WeekOptions = Readonly<{
  /** First day of the week. Default: `"monday"` (ISO 8601). */
  weekStartsOn?: Weekday | WeekdayNumber | undefined;
  /** Days that `isWeekend` counts as weekend. Default: `["saturday", "sunday"]`. */
  weekend?: readonly (Weekday | WeekdayNumber)[] | undefined;
}>;
```

Week options every adapter factory accepts.

### `Weekday`

Same as `Weekday` in `minuta`.

### `WeekdayNumber`

```ts
type WeekdayNumber =
  | typeof SUNDAY
  | typeof MONDAY
  | typeof TUESDAY
  | typeof WEDNESDAY
  | typeof THURSDAY
  | typeof FRIDAY
  | typeof SATURDAY;
```

A day of the week as `Date#getDay()` numbers it: 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday.

### `AllUnits`

```ts
type AllUnits = Readonly<Record<Unit, UnitSpec>> & Settings;
```

A spec for every unit, as returned by the adapters.

### `Period`

Same as `Period` in `minuta`.

### `Series`

Same as `Series` in `minuta`.

### `Unit`

Same as `Unit` in `minuta`.

### `UnitRegistry`

Registry of unit names. An interface so plugins can add units through
module augmentation; the matching spec is passed as data in `Units`.

### `Units`

Same as `Units` in `minuta`.

### `UnitSpec`

```ts
type UnitSpec = Readonly<{
  add: (date: Readonly<Date>, amount: number) => Date;
  diff: (from: Readonly<Date>, to: Readonly<Date>) => number;
  endOf: (date: Readonly<Date>) => Date;
  startOf: (date: Readonly<Date>) => Date;
}>;
```

How one unit behaves — plain data, like a country spec in ibanita.

- startOf: earliest millisecond of the unit containing `date`
- endOf: latest millisecond of the unit containing `date`
- add(date, n) then add(result, -n) returns the original date
- diff(from, to) is the number of complete units from `from` to `to`,
  truncated toward zero: the largest `n` with `add(from, n) <= to` (for an
  earlier `to`, the smallest `n` with `add(from, n) >= to`). The adapters
  guarantee it; custom units must follow it

## `minuta/calendar`

### `calendar`

```ts
const calendar: Readonly<{
  dayGrid: typeof dayGridWith;
  monthGrid: typeof monthGridWith;
  yearGrid: typeof yearGridWith;
}>
```

The calendar plugin: pass it to `withUnits(units, { plugins: [calendar] })`
or to `bind(units, calendar)`.

### `dayGridWith`

```ts
dayGridWith(units: Units, date: Readonly<Date>): DayGrid
```

The real hours of the day containing `date`: 23 on a spring-forward day,
25 on a fall-back day, 24 otherwise. Each slot carries its wall-clock hour
in `units.timeZone` (the runtime's zone when unset).

```ts
import { dateFnsTzUnits } from "minuta/date-fns-tz";
import { dayGridWith } from "minuta/calendar";

const units = dateFnsTzUnits({ timeZone: "America/New_York" });
const { periods, gapHour } = dayGridWith(units, new Date("2024-03-10T12:00:00Z"));
periods.length; // 23
gapHour; // 2
```

### `monthGridWith`

```ts
monthGridWith(units: Units, date: Readonly<Date>): MonthGrid
```

A stable month grid: 42 day periods (6 weeks) starting with the week that
contains the first of the month. The week start comes from the `week` unit.

```ts
const { periods } = monthGridWith(nativeUnits({ weekStartsOn: "monday" }), new Date(2026, 2, 15));
```

### `yearGridWith`

```ts
yearGridWith(units: Units, date: Readonly<Date>): YearGrid
```

A stable year grid: whole weeks from the week containing January 1 to the
week containing December 31. The week start comes from the `week` unit.

```ts
yearGridWith(nativeUnits({ weekStartsOn: "monday" }), new Date(2026, 5, 1)).periods; // 53 week periods
```

### `DayGrid`

```ts
type DayGrid = Readonly<{
  /** The slots; a DayGrid is also a `Series` */
  periods: readonly HourSlot[];
  /** Wall-clock hour that doesn't exist due to spring forward, or undefined */
  gapHour: number | undefined;
  /** Wall-clock hour that occurs twice due to fall back, or undefined */
  ambiguousHour: number | undefined;
}>;
```

The real hours of a day: 23, 24 or 25 slots, with DST metadata.

### `HourSlot`

```ts
type HourSlot = Period &
  Readonly<{
    /** Wall-clock hour (0-23) in the units' time zone */
    hour: number;
  }>;
```

One real hour of a day, labelled with its wall-clock hour.

### `MonthGrid`

```ts
type MonthGrid = Series &
  Readonly<{
    monthStart: Readonly<Date>;
    weekStartsOn: number;
  }>;
```

A 42-day month grid (`periods`), the month's first day and the week start
the grid was built with.

### `YearGrid`

```ts
type YearGrid = Series &
  Readonly<{
    weekStartsOn: number;
    yearStart: Readonly<Date>;
  }>;
```

The whole weeks covering a year (`periods`), the year's first day and the
week start the grid was built with.

## `minuta/format`

### `formatPeriod`

```ts
formatPeriod(period: Period, locale: string, options: DisplayOptions = {}): string
```

Format a period as a locale-aware display string.

Uses Intl.DateTimeFormat — zero locale data shipped.
Automatically picks the right format based on period type.

```ts
// month period, de-CH
formatPeriod(monthPeriod, "de-CH")
// → "März 2026"

// day period, en-US
formatPeriod(dayPeriod, "en-US")
// → "March 15, 2026"

// week period, ja-JP
formatPeriod(weekPeriod, "ja-JP")
// → "2026/03/09～2026/03/15"

// a period of time-zone units, in their zone
formatPeriod(tokyoDay, "en-US", { timeZone: tokyo.timeZone })
```

### `formatPeriodWith`

```ts
formatPeriodWith(period: Period, locale: string, options: DisplayOptions): string
```

Format a period with explicit Intl options.

Escape hatch for custom formatting needs.

```ts
formatPeriodWith(period, "de-CH", { weekday: "long", day: "numeric" })
// → "Sonntag, 15."
```

### `formatRange`

```ts
formatRange(period: Period, locale: string, options: DisplayOptions = {}): string
```

Format a period as a locale-aware range string.

Uses Intl.DateTimeFormat.formatRange() which intelligently collapses
shared parts (same year, same month).

```ts
// Same month: "1.–31. März 2026"
// Cross month: "30. März – 5. Apr. 2026"
// Cross year: "29. Dez. 2025 – 4. Jan. 2026"
```

## `minuta/native`

### `nativeUnits`

```ts
nativeUnits(options: WeekOptions = {}): AllUnits
```

Unit specs for every unit, computed with the built-in `Date` (zero dependencies). Pass the result to
`withUnits`, to any `…With` function in `minuta/core`, or to a plugin via
`bind`. Weeks start on Monday unless `weekStartsOn` says otherwise
(`"sunday"` … `"saturday"`, or 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday); `weekend` sets
the days `isWeekend` counts (Saturday and Sunday unless set).

```ts
import { nativeUnits } from "minuta/native";
import { withUnits } from "minuta/core";

const time = withUnits(nativeUnits({ weekStartsOn: "sunday" }));
time.period(new Date(), "week");
```

dateFnsUnits(options: WeekOptions = {}): AllUnits

## `minuta/date-fns-tz`

### `dateFnsTzUnits`

```ts
dateFnsTzUnits(options: WeekOptions & Readonly<{ timeZone?: string }> = {}): AllUnits
```

Unit specs for every unit, computed with date-fns-tz in one IANA time zone (requires `date-fns` and `date-fns-tz`). Pass the result to
`withUnits`, to any `…With` function in `minuta/core`, or to a plugin via
`bind`. Weeks start on Monday unless `weekStartsOn` says otherwise
(`"sunday"` … `"saturday"`, or 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday); `weekend` sets
the days `isWeekend` counts (Saturday and Sunday unless set).

```ts

time.period(new Date(), "week");
```
